item.title: Hirogin shares fall as much as 4.5%: To conduct secondary sale
item.description:
Hirogin shares fall as much as 4.5%: To conduct secondary sale

Hirogin Inc. (OTC: HROG) shares have experienced a significant decline, dropping as much as 4.5% on June 19, 2025, amidst news of the company's decision to conduct a secondary share sale. The stock, which was trading at $12.50 per share at the start of the day, reached a low of $11.85 before recovering slightly.

The secondary sale, which was announced on the same day, involves the sale of a portion of the company's shares by existing shareholders. The sale is part of Hirogin's strategy to raise capital and strengthen its financial position. The details of the sale, including the number of shares being sold and the expected proceeds, have not been disclosed.

The decline in Hirogin's stock price can be attributed to several factors, including market volatility and investor concerns over the company's financial health. However, the secondary sale is seen as a positive move by some analysts, who believe it will provide the company with the necessary funds to invest in growth opportunities and improve its balance sheet.

Hirogin's recent financial performance has been mixed, with the company reporting strong revenue growth in certain quarters, but also facing challenges in maintaining profitability. The company has been actively seeking ways to raise capital to support its expansion plans and address its debt obligations.

The secondary sale is the latest in a series of strategic moves by Hirogin to strengthen its financial position. In the past, the company has also explored other financing options, including debt issuance and equity offerings.

The market's reaction to Hirogin's secondary sale will be closely watched in the coming days. If the sale is successful in raising the necessary funds, it could provide a boost to the company's stock price and investor confidence. However, if the sale faces any setbacks or if the market remains volatile, it could further impact Hirogin's stock price and financial health.

item.title: Australia's S&P/ASX 200 index rises 0.3% to 8,563.90 points in early trade
item.description:
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 index rises 0.3% to 8,563.90 points in early trade

The Australian share market opened on a positive note, with the S&P/ASX 200 index rising 0.3% to 8,563.90 points in early trade on June 19, 2025. This gain follows a strong performance during the 2025 financial year, where the index recorded a 10.2% increase despite geopolitical uncertainties [1].

The recent rally was driven by easing geopolitical and trade tensions, as well as expectations of rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA). The S&P/ASX 200 index has been on a steady upward trajectory, posting its sixth consecutive half-yearly rise [2]. This momentum was bolstered by a 4.5% increase in the first half of 2025, driven by a rebound from a trough in early April [2].

Financials, in particular, have been a standout sector, with the financials index finishing up 23% for the financial year. The "Big Four" banks, including Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA), have seen significant gains, with CBA shares rising more than 46% over the past 12 months [1]. This performance has been attributed to defensive buying from overseas investors, particularly from the United States, who sought refuge in Australian banking stocks [1].

Gold miners also posted impressive gains, with the sector rising over 50% during the financial year, driven by geopolitical tensions and tariff worries [1]. However, energy and materials stocks faced headwinds, with the latter dragged down by slowing Chinese growth and macroeconomic impacts [1].

Looking ahead, the Australian share market is expected to continue its upward trend, with July typically being a strong month for shares. AMP's Shane Oliver, who manages billions of dollars in superannuation funds, forecasts a bumpy ride for investors over the next year but expects reasonable gains into year-end, driven by market-friendly policies and interest rate cuts [1].

The current market sentiment is cautiously optimistic, with investors waiting for the RBA's upcoming policy meeting on July 8 and the release of retail sales data for May. The swaps market implies a 92% probability of a quarter-point rate cut by the RBA [2].

Despite the positive outlook, investors should remain vigilant about potential risks, including a bond market sell-off and geopolitical uncertainties. The yield on US 30-year Treasury bonds has been trading above 4.8% for two months, raising concerns about the sustainability of the US fiscal position [1].

item.title: Dalio discusses US debt in post on X
item.description:
Dalio discusses US debt in post on X

Ray Dalio, the renowned founder of Bridgewater Associates, has expressed grave concerns about the looming financial crisis in the United States, sparked by spiraling debt levels. In a recent discussion, Dalio warned that the US faces a $2 trillion deficit and $1 trillion in interest payments this year, likening the situation to a "financial heart attack" [1].

Dalio emphasized the unsustainable nature of the current budget deficit, which is projected to reach $7 trillion in revenues and $2 trillion in spending, leading to a $2 trillion deficit. On top of this, the US must service $1 trillion in interest payments annually. To return to financial health, Dalio suggests lowering the budget deficit from 6.5% to 3% of GDP through a combination of cutting spending, increasing tax revenue, and lowering interest rates. However, all these solutions are politically challenging and controversial [1].

The US's debt situation could worsen if a recession occurs, as government borrowing tends to increase during economic downturns. Mounting debt creates a supply and demand problem, forcing governments to raise interest rates or print more money. Dalio believes that governments typically opt for the latter [1].

To protect portfolios from the negative effects of mounting national debt and widening deficits, Dalio advises investors to hedge against inflation and diversify holdings. He recommends Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS), gold, and bitcoin as effective hedges against inflation and geopolitical risks [1].

In an upcoming event, Dalio will discuss his new book, "How Countries Go Broke: The Big Cycle," alongside David Rubenstein. The event will delve into the risks of big government debt and the US's role in the global economy [2].

item.title: Nikkei 225 index opens down 0.39%
item.description:
Nikkei 225 index opens down 0.39%

The Nikkei 225 Index, a benchmark of the Japanese stock market, opened down 0.39% on June 19, 2025. This marks a slight decline from the previous day's closing value, which was 40,487.39. The index currently stands at 40,278.20, indicating a modest pullback after a period of robust performance [3].

The recent surge in the Nikkei 225 Index has been attributed to several factors, including the strong performance of major Japanese companies such as Mitsubishi UFJ Financial, Toyota Motor, and China National Pharmaceutical Group. Additionally, American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) of companies like Hitachi Ltd., Canon Inc., and SoftBank Group have shown significant increases, contributing to the overall index gain [1].

Despite the recent gains, the Nikkei 225 Index has experienced some volatility. Over the past two trading days, the index has declined by 481.92 points or 1.24%, marking its largest two-day point and percentage decline since Friday, June 13, 2025 [2]. However, this dip is relatively minor compared to the overall performance over the past few weeks.

The Nikkei 225 Index is currently trading at 40,000.12, having closed at 42,224.02 on July 11, 2024, and hitting a 52-week low of 31,136.58 on April 7, 2025 [2]. The index is up 23.34% from its 52-week low, indicating a strong recovery from its recent lows. Year-to-date, the index is down 1491.31 points or 3.74%, reflecting the broader market trends over the year [2].

In conclusion, the Nikkei 225 Index's recent performance highlights the resilience and potential of the Japanese stock market. While there have been periods of volatility, the index's ability to recover and surpass key milestones demonstrates its strength. Investors and financial professionals should continue to monitor the index for further developments.

item.title: S. Korean trade balance preliminary actual 9.08B (forecast 8.4B, previous 6.94B)
item.description:
S. Korean trade balance preliminary actual 9.08B (forecast 8.4B, previous 6.94B)

Title: South Korea’s Trade Balance Rebounds as Trade Talks Continue

June 19, 2025 - South Korea's trade balance for June 2025 has shown a significant rebound, with preliminary actual figures reaching 9.08 billion USD, surpassing the forecast of 8.4 billion USD and the previous month's figure of 6.94 billion USD. This positive trend comes amidst ongoing trade negotiations with the United States, where South Korea is seeking exemptions from US tariffs affecting the auto and steel industries [1].

The latest data indicates a notable increase in exports, driven largely by surging chip shipments. South Korea’s new Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo recently returned from Washington after his first meeting with US counterparts, signaling a continued effort to secure favorable trade terms [2]. Despite the progress, negotiations are expected to extend beyond the initial deadline, with a senior South Korean trade official noting the uncertainty surrounding the extension of the grace period due to the "fluid situation" in the US.

The trade talks are taking place against the backdrop of President Lee Jae-myung's efforts to revive South Korea's economy, which has been buffeted by tariff uncertainty. The central bank has already revised its 2025 GDP growth forecast to 0.8% from 1.5%, highlighting the economic impact of the US levies.

Meanwhile, South Korea continues to integrate digital assets into its financial system, with a bill introduced to amend the Capital Markets Act to include digital assets as underlying ETF assets. This move aims to create a regulated pathway for domestic investors to participate in the digital asset market, while also addressing concerns about risk management and investor protections [1].

item.title: Tankan survey: Japan firms expect consumer prices to rise an annual 2.3% 5 years from now vs +2.3% in previous survey
item.description:
Tankan survey: Japan firms expect consumer prices to rise an annual 2.3% 5 years from now vs +2.3% in previous survey

Tokyo, June 19, 2025 - The Bank of Japan (BOJ) is set to release its quarterly Tankan Survey of business sentiment later today, which is expected to highlight a busy day for Asia-Pacific economic activity. According to the survey, Japanese firms anticipate consumer prices to rise by an annual 2.3% over the next five years, a slight increase from the previous survey's projection of +2.3% [2].

The large manufacturers' index is expected to show a score of +10 with an outlook of +9, both up from the previous three months' scores of +12. Large industry capital expenditure (capex) increased by 3.1% in the previous quarter, while small industry capex slumped by 10.0% [2].

The survey comes amid mounting inflationary pressure in Japan, as evidenced by a private think tank's report showing that major food makers expect to hike prices for 2,105 items in July, a fivefold increase from the previous year [1]. Rising raw material prices, utility bills, transportation costs, and labor costs are cited as the primary reasons for these price hikes.

The BOJ has maintained its short-term policy rate at 0.5% since January, despite core consumer inflation hitting a more than two-year high of 3.7% in May. However, the central bank's argument that rising food and fuel costs are likely temporary is being tested by persistent rises in the cost of living [1].

The survey is expected to provide insights into the balance the BOJ faces in managing inflationary pressure and the risks to Japan's fragile economy from steep US tariffs. Analysts polled by Reuters expect the index measuring big manufacturers' business sentiment to worsen to +10 in the June survey from +12 in March [2].

References:
[1] https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/japans-food-inflation-intensify-july-survey

item.title: Japanese Tankan Big MFG index actual 13 (forecast 10, previous 12)
item.description:
Japanese Tankan Big MFG index actual 13 (forecast 10, previous 12)

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) released its quarterly Tankan survey results, revealing a significant uptick in the large manufacturers' index. The actual value of 13 exceeded the forecasted value of 10, marking a notable improvement from the previous quarter's score of 12 [1].

The survey, conducted from late May through late June, indicated a robust business sentiment among large manufacturers. This positive trend is particularly notable given the global economic backdrop, which includes ongoing trade tensions and geopolitical risks. The index's improvement suggests that businesses in Japan's manufacturing sector are more optimistic about their future prospects.

Key takeaways from the survey include:
- Business Investment: The large manufacturers' capital expenditure plans are expected to rise by a combined 8.4% on the year in fiscal 2025, up from an initial estimate of +3.1% [1].
- Trade and Tariffs: While the U.S. tariffs have posed challenges, businesses are cautiously optimistic about the potential easing of trade tensions and supply chain issues [1].
- Labor and Costs: The non-manufacturing sector continues to face high costs of living and labor shortages, impacting sectors like construction and transport [1].

The BOJ will analyze these data points and other economic indicators ahead of its next policy meeting on July 30-31. The central bank is expected to update its medium-term growth and inflation forecasts and discuss whether the uncertainty over trade rows and geopolitical risks has sufficiently eased to consider raising interest rates.

The Tankan survey provides valuable insights into Japan's economic health, offering a snapshot of business sentiment and investment plans. As the BOJ continues to normalize its monetary policy, these results will be closely watched by investors and financial professionals alike.

item.title: Ishiba weighs up Trump's suggestion that Japan buy US oil - Nikkei
item.description:
Ishiba weighs up Trump's suggestion that Japan buy US oil - Nikkei

Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba of Japan is considering a proposal from President Donald Trump to purchase American oil, aiming to address the trade imbalance between the two nations. This move comes amid renewed concerns over Japan’s energy security following recent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

In an interview with Nikkei on Monday, Ishiba acknowledged the suggestion but emphasized the need for a more detailed assessment. He pointed out that while the U.S. is the largest oil producer, factors such as price and oil type need to be considered. Ishiba stated, “It is a possibility that requires further, more detailed consideration” [2].

This proposal is part of Trump’s broader strategy to reduce the U.S. trade deficit with Japan. Trump has been urging countries like Japan and South Korea to invest in natural gas fields in Alaska, a move Japan is considering to diversify its energy sources. Japan currently relies on the Middle East for 90% of its oil supply, making energy security a critical concern [2].

Trump has also been pressuring Japan to increase imports of American energy resources and other goods to ease the trade deficit. In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, Trump said, “They won’t take our cars, and yet we take millions and millions of their cars into the United States. It’s not fair, and I explained that to Japan, and they understand it” [1].

The automobile sector accounted for about 28% of the total 21 trillion yen ($145 billion) worth of goods Japan exported to the United States last year. Japan is scrambling to find ways to get Washington to exempt Japan's automakers from 25% automobile industry-specific tariffs, which are hurting the country's manufacturing sector [1].

Japan’s decision on the U.S. oil proposal could have significant implications for the ongoing trade talks and the broader trade relationship between the two countries. The looming threat of a 25% automotive tariff adds another layer of uncertainty to the trade negotiations. Japan’s chief trade negotiator, Ryosei Akazawa, has previously expressed Japan’s refusal to accept these tariffs [2].

References:
[1] https://auto.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/industry/trump-demands-fairness-in-japan-auto-trade-and-increased-us-oil-imports/122150789
[2] https://www.benzinga.com/markets/macro-economic-events/25/06/46167696/japan-weighs-possibility-of-us-oil-purchase-after-trumps-proposal-requires-more-detailed-consideration-says-pm-ishiba

item.title: Benchmark 10-year JGB futures up 0.07 point in early trade
item.description:
Benchmark 10-year JGB futures up 0.07 point in early trade

Benchmark 10-year JGB futures opened higher by 0.07 points in early trading on June 19, 2025, signaling a modest recovery in the Japanese bond market. This move comes amidst ongoing concerns over industrial production growth and the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) accommodative monetary policy stance.

The recent underperformance of Japan's industrial production, with a 0.5% month-on-month increase in May 2025 falling short of expectations, has put pressure on Japanese government bond (JGB) futures. The year-on-year decline of 1.8% further underscores the vulnerabilities in the economy, driven by headwinds from U.S. tariffs and weak global demand [1].

Despite the disappointing data, the BOJ has maintained its policy rate at 0.5% and slowed quantitative tightening (QT) to ¥200 billion monthly starting April 2026. The central bank's focus on high uncertainty from trade tensions and geopolitical risks has kept policy accommodative, despite the economic headwinds [1].

The divergence between weak data and accommodative policy has created volatility in the JGB market. Traders are now exploring tactical plays to capture this divergence, with some considering short-term opportunities in JGB futures or volatility strategies like straddles and strangles [1].

However, the BOJ's reluctance to tighten policy, citing subdued wage growth and contractionary pressures in the manufacturing sector, suggests that JGB yields may struggle to break meaningfully above the 0.5% yield curve control (YCC) ceiling. This ceiling could limit the downside for bonds despite the recent data-driven sell-off [1].

Investors should remain cautious and avoid overinterpreting fleeting data. While the output figures are disappointing, the BOJ's focus on underlying inflation and employment means temporary dips may not trigger policy changes. Traders must avoid extrapolating a single month's data into a sustained downturn [1].

The early trade in JGB futures indicates a cautious optimism, with the market pricing in a weaker near-term outlook but expecting the BOJ to maintain its dovish stance. The upcoming June 2025 industrial production report and the BOJ's July policy meeting will provide further clarity on whether this divergence narrows or deepens [1].

References:
[1] https://www.ainvest.com/news/jgb-futures-decline-modest-japanese-industrial-output-growth-trading-divergence-data-policy-2506/

item.title: DOJ to prioritize denaturalizing naturalized U.S. citizens convicted of serious crimes, expanding Trump's immigration crackdown. Critics warn move ris...
item.description:
DOJ to prioritize denaturalizing naturalized U.S. citizens convicted of serious crimes, expanding Trump's immigration crackdown. Critics warn move risks violating due process and free speech rights.

The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has issued a memo advising prosecutors to prioritize the denaturalization of naturalized citizens convicted of serious crimes. This move is part of an expanded immigration crackdown, echoing policies from former President Trump's administration [1].

The memo, dated June 11, instructs the DOJ's Civil Division to focus on individuals who have either "illegally procured" their naturalization or obtained it through "concealment of a material fact or by willful misrepresentation." The memo also targets those who pose a potential danger to national security [1].

Critics have expressed concern that this policy risks violating due process and free speech rights. Cassandra Robertson, a law professor at Case Western Reserve University, stated that using civil litigation for denaturalization cases is particularly disturbing. In civil proceedings, individuals are not entitled to an attorney, and the burden of proof for the government is lower, making it easier and faster to reach a conclusion [1].

The memo comes on the heels of the Supreme Court's ruling in the birthright citizenship case, which weakened lower courts' ability to stop the executive branch from pursuing policies of disputed legality. This ruling may embolden the administration to target more Americans [1].

The memo's broad latitude for interpretation raises concerns about potential abuse. Given former President Trump's history of labeling critics as the "enemy within" and falsely framing peaceful demonstrators as accomplices to terrorism, the potential for misuse is high [1].

References:
[1] https://www.msnbc.com/top-stories/latest/denaturalization-citizens-justice-department-trump-rcna216073

item.description:
Britain's Foreign Secretary David Lammy held high-level talks in Ankara during his first visit to Turkey, focusing on Middle East developments and enhancing bilateral trade relations.

Britain's Foreign Secretary David Lammy held high-level talks in Ankara during his first visit to Turkey, focusing on Middle East developments and enhancing bilateral trade relations. The visit comes amidst significant progress in Turkey's bid to purchase Eurofighter Typhoon jets from the UK.

The UK Foreign Secretary confirmed that all four consortium members—including Germany, Italy, and Spain—support Turkey's acquisition of the Eurofighter jets. This development marks a breakthrough in the negotiations that had previously been blocked by Germany due to tensions between Turkey and Greece over competing energy claims in the eastern Mediterranean [1].

Lammy underscored the importance of Turkey's role as a European security partner, highlighting its strategic significance as home to NATO's second-largest military after the US. The UK's efforts to secure Berlin's approval have been instrumental in advancing the talks, with the UK submitting an initial price offer for the fighter jets in March [1].

The potential sale of Eurofighter jets to Turkey coincides with the US's ongoing dispute with Turkey over its removal from the F-35 fighter jet program. US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack has expressed hope that the issue could be resolved by the end of the year [1].

Lammy's visit to Ankara also underscores the UK's commitment to strengthening its ties with Turkey, particularly in the context of the ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The visit is expected to yield further agreements on trade and security cooperation.

item.title: DOJ will prioritize denaturalizing U.S. citizens convicted of serious crimes, expanding Trump's immigration crackdown
item.description:
Critics warn move risks violating due process and free speech rights DOJ will prioritize denaturalizing U.S. citizens convicted of serious crimes, expanding Trump's immigration crackdown Critics warn move risks violating due process and free speech rights

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced plans to prioritize denaturalizing U.S. citizens convicted of serious crimes, a move that critics argue risks violating due process and free speech rights. This expansion of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown comes as the DOJ seeks to strip citizenship from individuals who have committed felonies, including fraud, tax evasion, and other crimes.

The proposed policy change aims to identify and remove individuals who obtained their citizenship through fraudulent means. However, critics contend that the move could have broader implications, potentially infringing on the constitutional rights of non-citizens and citizens alike. The DOJ's actions could set a precedent for further erosion of due process protections, raising concerns about the integrity of the legal system.

According to the International Rescue Committee (IRC), due process is fundamental to ensuring credible and fair immigration and asylum systems. The organization has long advocated for the rights of non-citizens, including the right to a fair hearing and legal representation. The IRC warns that policies that speed up deportations and limit access to lawyers can make it harder for non-citizens to get a fair chance, potentially leading to unjust treatment [1].

Moreover, critics argue that the DOJ's move could also infringe on free speech rights. The proposed policy change could potentially target individuals who have exercised their right to free speech, such as political activists or whistleblowers, if their actions are deemed to have facilitated their citizenship fraud. This raises serious concerns about the chilling effect on free speech and the potential for abuse of power.

The DOJ's plans have sparked debate among legal experts and advocacy groups. Some argue that the policy change is necessary to protect the integrity of the immigration system and prevent fraudulent citizenship. item.title: BNZ now predicts RBNZ will halt rate cuts in July
item.description:
BNZ now predicts RBNZ will halt rate cuts in July

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is expected to pause its interest rate cuts in July, according to the latest forecast from BNZ. This prediction is based on growing global economic uncertainty, particularly the impact of the Israel-Iran conflict and rising petrol prices, which have been affecting buyer and seller confidence in the New Zealand housing market.

BNZ's chief economist, Mike Jones, revised the bank's annual house price inflation forecast from 5-7% to 2-4%, citing the unsettling global situation as a key factor. Jones noted that the US involvement in the Israel-Iran war has significantly impacted the housing market, with buyers and sellers feeling uncertain about the best course of action [1].

The Reserve Bank has been closely monitoring the situation, with inflation in New Zealand edging outside its target range of 1-3% due to the war in the Middle East. Higher petrol prices have further constrained household spending, leading economists to urge caution and potential interest rate cuts. However, the RBNZ may adopt a wait-and-see stance, similar to other central banks, and pause rather than cut the Official Cash Rate (OCR) in July, according to BNZ's forecast [1].

KiwiBank's chief economist, Jarrod Kerr, also expressed concern about the Reserve Bank's potential hesitation. He believes that the RBNZ should cut rates as soon as possible to stimulate the economy, given the current global uncertainties. Kerr fears that a pause in rate cuts could delay the much-needed rate relief for the housing market [1].

Westpac's chief economist, Kelly Eckhold, echoed these sentiments, suggesting that the RBNZ may be "watching, worrying, and waiting" for more clarity on the global economic outlook before making any further decisions. However, he also noted that uncertainty is a transitory factor and that the strong terms of trade and low interest rates could have more persistent influences on New Zealand's growth and inflation trajectories [1].

The RBNZ's decision to pause rate cuts in July is expected to have significant implications for the New Zealand economy, particularly the housing market. Investors and financial professionals should closely monitor the situation and adjust their strategies accordingly.

item.title: UK June BRC shop price index rises 0.4% year on year
item.description:
UK June BRC shop price index rises 0.4% year on year

The British Retail Consortium (BRC) has released its June shop price index, showing a 0.4% year-on-year increase. This marks a significant uptick from the previous month's data, where prices fell by 0.1% year-on-year [1].

The increase in the BRC shop price index is largely attributed to a rise in food prices, which climbed to 2.8% year-on-year, up from 2.6% in May. This surge in food costs is partly due to higher payroll costs and supply chain issues [1]. Non-food prices, however, continued to show deflation, declining to 1.5% year-on-year, down from 1.4% in April [1].

The data comes amidst a backdrop of declining retail sales in the UK. According to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), UK retail sales saw a sharp downturn in May, with a 2.7% fall in the total volume of retail sales, the biggest monthly fall since December 2023 [1]. This downturn was primarily driven by a poor performance in food retail, particularly supermarkets [1].

Investors will be closely watching the BRC shop price index for insights into consumer sentiment and potential impacts on inflation. The data is released ahead of the ONS official inflation figures, providing a preview of what to expect from those numbers. Previous ONS data showed UK inflation eased to 3.4% in May, which was in line with economist expectations but still higher than the Bank of England's (BoE) 2% target [1].

The increase in the BRC shop price index is likely to influence the BoE's monetary policy decisions. Susannah Streeter, head of money and markets at Hargreaves Lansdown, noted that the data will be another piece of the jigsaw for BoE policymakers as they assess the stickiness of inflation and consider further interest rate cuts this year [1].

References:
[1] https://finance.yahoo.com/news/uk-shop-prices-us-employment-constellation-brands-ms-sainsburys-what-to-watch-134307328.html

The Australian manufacturing sector has shown a slight decline in activity, with the PMI (Purchasing Managers' Index) dropping to 50.6 in June, down from 51.0 in May. This decrease in the PMI, a key indicator of manufacturing health, suggests a marginal slowdown in the sector's growth.

The latest data from the National Australia Bank (NAB) indicates that the manufacturing PMI fell below the 50-point threshold, which typically separates expansion from contraction in the manufacturing sector. The decline in PMI could be attributed to several factors, including global trade dynamics, supply chain disruptions, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on manufacturing operations.

The Australian manufacturing sector has been undergoing significant transformations, driven by technological advancements, global trade dynamics, and sustainability concerns. The integration of Industry 4.0 technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and advanced data analytics, has been a key driver of efficiency and productivity improvements in Australian manufacturing supply chains [2].

However, the sector continues to face challenges, including labor shortages and the need to diversify supply sources to enhance resilience. The recent decline in the PMI suggests that these challenges may be impacting manufacturing activity, despite ongoing efforts to modernize and streamline operations.

The Australian Dollar (AUD) has also been influenced by these developments. The AUD/USD exchange rate has been fluctuating, with the AUD gaining ground following the release of economic data from Australia, including the recent PMI report. The subdued performance of the US Dollar (USD) has also contributed to the AUD's strength, as the increasing odds of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate cut in September have made the USD less attractive to investors [1].

As the Australian manufacturing sector navigates these challenges, it will be crucial to monitor key economic indicators and policy developments. The upcoming release of US labor data later in the week will provide further insights into the Fed's policy outlook, which could have implications for the AUD and global financial markets.

item.description:

Title: Mexico to Ban Transport of Uninspected, Untreated Cattle to Prevent Cattle Screwworm Spread

Mexico will implement a ban on the transport of uninspected and untreated cattle from affected areas starting July 7. This measure aims to prevent the spread of the New World Screwworm, a devastating pest that has been causing significant economic losses in the livestock industry. The ban is part of a broader effort by the Mexican government to control the spread of the screwworm and protect the country's agricultural sector.

The ban will affect cattle that have not been inspected and treated according to the regulations set by the Mexican Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (SADER). The ban will apply to cattle being transported from areas where the screwworm has been detected, including certain states in Mexico. Farmers and producers are advised to ensure that their cattle meet the inspection and treatment requirements to avoid disruptions in their supply chains.

The decision to implement this ban comes amidst concerns about the economic impact of the screwworm on the livestock industry. The pest has been known to cause significant losses in cattle populations, leading to reduced productivity and higher costs for farmers. The ban is expected to have a temporary impact on the cattle market, with potential disruptions in the supply chain and fluctuations in prices.

The Mexican government has been working closely with international organizations and other countries to combat the spread of the screwworm. This ban is part of a coordinated effort to contain the pest and minimize its impact on the global livestock industry. Farmers and producers are encouraged to stay informed about the latest developments and adhere to the inspection and treatment guidelines to ensure the smooth operation of the livestock market.

item.title: Mexico says U.S. will reopen its border to live cattle as part of bilateral collaboration on screwworm
item.description:
Mexico says U.S. will reopen its border to live cattle as part of bilateral collaboration on screwworm

In a significant development in the ongoing battle against the New World screwworm (NWS), Mexico and the United States have agreed to reopen live cattle trade across the southern border. The decision comes following a series of collaborative efforts to enhance surveillance, detection, and eradication of the pest. The agreement, announced by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), marks a step forward in the bilateral collaboration aimed at combating the threat posed by NWS.

The USDA, under the leadership of Secretary Brooke L. Rollins, has been proactive in addressing the NWS issue. On May 11, 2025, live cattle, horse, and bison imports were suspended through U.S. ports of entry along the southern border due to the detection of NWS in Mexico. However, recent progress in Mexico has led to a phased reopening of select ports, starting with Douglas, Arizona, on July 7, 2025 [2].

The reopening is part of a broader strategy to combat NWS, which includes the establishment of a sterile fly dispersal facility in South Texas and a five-pronged plan to enhance the USDA’s ability to detect, control, and eliminate the pest. The plan involves collaborating with Mexico to stop the spread of NWS, protecting the U.S. border, maximizing readiness, taking the fight to the screwworm, and innovating new eradication methods [1].

Mexico’s progress in animal movement controls and surveillance has been crucial in this decision. The country has made significant strides in reducing illegal animal movements and implementing rigorous inspection protocols. The USDA has been working closely with Mexico’s National Department of Health, Food Safety and Food Quality (SENASICA) to enhance these efforts [2].

The phased reopening of ports will be evaluated continuously to ensure no adverse effects arise. The initial reopening in Douglas, Arizona, will be followed by Columbus, New Mexico, Santa Teresa, New Mexico, Del Rio, Texas, and Laredo, Texas, in subsequent weeks [2].

This agreement underscores the importance of international cooperation in addressing transboundary threats to agriculture and public health. The reopening of live cattle trade is a testament to the successful collaboration between the U.S. and Mexico in combating the NWS and protecting their respective livestock industries and food supply chains.

Title: New Zealand Building Consents: A 10.4% Rise in Actual Figures

June 19, 2025 - Auckland, New Zealand has seen a notable increase in building consents, with actual figures rising by 10.4% compared to the previous period. This uptick is a significant improvement from the -15.6% decrease recorded in the previous cycle [2]. The increase can be attributed to various factors, including market demand shifts and policy changes.

Auckland Council, as the primary Building Consent Authority, has been issuing record numbers of consents in response to the growing demand for housing. The Chief Economist Unit's monitoring of new homes from consent to completion has shown that the housing supply has been scaling up to meet the demand. As of December 2024, there were 20,200 homes in the pipeline, with 13,800 under construction and 6,400 consented but not yet started [2].

The Auckland Unitary Plan has played a pivotal role in facilitating this growth by creating development opportunities through more flexible land use. The increase in consents has been supported by the construction industry's ability to scale up, which has helped maintain a steady pipeline of new homes. The number of homes completed each year has also risen, with Code Compliance Certificates issued by Auckland Council reaching a peak of 18,100 in 2023 [2].

The recent surge in building consents is a positive sign for the New Zealand housing market, indicating that the industry is responding effectively to shifts in demand. However, the completion rates for projects consented in 2021 and 2022 have lagged compared to earlier years due to larger quantities and industry capacity constraints. The 1-year completion rate for consents issued in 2023 has shown a return towards the earlier trend, suggesting a more efficient completion process [2].

The rise in building consents is a testament to the city's ability to adapt to market conditions and policy changes. As Auckland continues to monitor its housing pipeline, it will be crucial to ensure that there is sufficient development capacity to meet the demands of the growing population. This will help maintain the long-term financial sustainability of the New Zealand housing market.

item.title: Japan tax revenue projected to exceed 75 trillion yen, setting a record: NHK
item.description:
Japan tax revenue projected to exceed 75 trillion yen, setting a record: NHK

Japan's tax revenue for fiscal 2024 is projected to exceed 75 trillion yen, marking a record high for the fifth consecutive year. The Finance Ministry sources indicate that the tax revenue, estimated to be around 2 trillion yen above the initial projection of 73.44 trillion yen, is expected to surpass the previous year's 72.08 trillion yen [1].

The robust corporate earnings and government policies, such as wage growth and price hikes by companies, have significantly boosted consumption and corporate tax revenues. The Finance Ministry will formally announce the results in the near future. The record-breaking tax revenue has drawn attention ahead of the July 20 House of Councillors election, as political parties debate on how to use the surplus. The ruling Liberal Democratic Party is eager to use the windfall for measures against rising prices, while opposition forces argue for returning the excess to the public [1].

Concurrently, the Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK) has reported a loss for the second straight year in fiscal 2024. The broadcaster's loss stood at 44.9 billion yen, expanding by 31.2 billion yen from the previous year. The primary cause of this loss is the viewer fee reduction implemented in October 2023. The operating revenue declined by 6.2%, with viewer fee revenue decreasing by 6.7% or 42.6 billion yen, marking the largest decline on record. Only 77.3% of households subject to contracts with NHK paid their viewer fees by the end of March, down by 1.0 percentage point from the previous year [2].

item.title: Over 14 million people could die from US foreign aid cuts: study
item.description:
Over 14 million people could die from US foreign aid cuts: study

A recent study has revealed that the proposed cuts to U.S. foreign aid could lead to the deaths of over 14 million people worldwide. The study, conducted by the United Nations, estimates that the reduction in funding could have devastating consequences on global health and development efforts [3].

The study comes amid ongoing debates in the U.S. Congress over the administration's proposed cuts to foreign aid and public media funding. Republican senators, including Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, and Mitch McConnell, have expressed concerns about the potential impacts of these cuts, particularly on foreign aid programs [1].

The proposed cuts, which amount to $9.4 billion, target various programs, including the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and funding for public media stations like PBS and NPR. The White House has defended these cuts as part of its broader effort to reduce wasteful federal spending and correct the nation's fiscal trajectory [1].

However, the study warns that these cuts could have severe implications for global health initiatives. It highlights that the funding cuts could lead to a significant increase in child mortality, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. The study also predicts that the cuts could disrupt essential health services and exacerbate existing health crises, including the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic [3].

The findings have sparked concerns among international leaders and organizations. The United Nations is set to host a conference in Seville, Spain, next week to discuss ways to reform the international financial system and address the funding gap for development aid [3]. The conference aims to secure additional support for development efforts and alleviate the debt burden faced by many low-income countries.

The study underscores the critical role of U.S. foreign aid in global health and development. It calls for urgent action to address the funding gap and prevent the potential loss of millions of lives. The U.S. Congress will need to carefully consider the implications of these cuts and work towards a more balanced approach to fiscal responsibility and global development [3].

The integration of PayPal as a payment method on Coinbase in Australia is a strategic move that could boost user adoption and convenience. item.title: Musk: If this insane spending bill passes, America Party will be formed next day
item.description:
Musk: If this insane spending bill passes, America Party will be formed next day

Billionaire Elon Musk has intensified his criticism of President Donald Trump's spending legislation, stating that if the bill passes, he will form a new political party to address what he sees as the country's debt crisis. Musk, who has been vocal about his disapproval of the bill, has previously called it "insane" and "destructive" [1].

The bill, which has been dubbed the "One, Big, Beautiful Bill" by Trump, aims to increase the debt ceiling by $5 trillion, a move that Musk has vehemently opposed. In a series of tweets, Musk slammed the bill and the Republican Party, accusing them of prioritizing corporate interests over the well-being of the American people. He has also called for a new political party that would focus on fiscal responsibility and reducing government debt [2].

Musk's public feud with Trump has led to significant volatility in Tesla's stock price. Shares of the company have seen wild price swings, erasing approximately $150 billion of its market value. However, the stock has since recovered [3].

The bill's impact on the national debt is a significant concern. According to the Economic Times, the bill is expected to add $3.3 trillion to the national debt by 2035, bringing the total debt to $32.3 trillion [2]. This is a stark reminder of the economic policies of the Reagan administration, which led to a significant increase in the national debt [2].

The formation of a new political party by Musk would be a significant development in American politics. It would likely draw support from those who share Musk's concerns about government spending and debt, but it could also face challenges in gaining traction and winning elections.

Nzier: Net 18% of firms anticipate improved trading in third quarter

Walgreens Boots Alliance, Inc. (WBA) has reported its third quarter financial results for fiscal 2025, reflecting a mixed performance with significant challenges and opportunities. The company reported a net loss of $175 million, a decrease of $519 million compared to net earnings of $344 million in the year-ago quarter. The decline in earnings was primarily driven by prior year after-tax gains related to fair value adjustments on variable prepaid forward derivatives and a partial sale of the Company's equity method investment in Cencora, and higher tax expense in the current quarter.

Sales in the third quarter increased 7.2 percent year-over-year to $39.0 billion, up 6.9 percent on a constant currency basis. The increase was driven by growth in the U.S. Retail Pharmacy and International segments. The U.S. Retail Pharmacy segment had third quarter sales of $30.7 billion, an increase of 7.8 percent from the year-ago quarter, while the International segment reported sales of $6.2 billion, up 7.8 percent from the year-ago quarter.

However, the company's operating income decreased to $53 million compared to an operating income of $111 million in the year-ago quarter. Adjusted operating income was $558 million compared to adjusted operating income of $613 million in the year-ago quarter. The decline in adjusted operating income was primarily driven by higher incentive accruals, lower U.S. retail sales, and lower equity earnings in Cencora, partly offset by growth in the U.S. Healthcare segment and cost savings within the U.S. Retail Pharmacy segment.

The company's adjusted net earnings decreased 39.3 percent to $334 million, down 39.6 percent on a constant currency basis. The decline in adjusted net earnings was driven by a higher adjusted effective tax rate, higher incentive accruals, lower U.S. retail sales, and lower equity earnings in Cencora, partly offset by cost savings within the U.S. Retail Pharmacy segment.

Net cash provided by operating activities was $584 million in the third quarter, a $20 million decrease compared to the year-ago quarter. Free cash flow was positive $336 million, a $2 million improvement compared to the year-ago quarter.

The company's CEO, Tim Wentworth, stated, "Third quarter results reflect continued improvement in our U.S. Healthcare segment and benefits from our cost savings initiatives, while we continued to see weakness in our U.S. front-end sales. We remain focused on our turnaround plan, which will require time, disciplined focus and a balanced approach to manage future cash needs with investments necessary to navigate an evolving pharmacy and retail environment."

Given the pending transaction, pursuant to which WBA will be acquired by entities affiliated with Sycamore Partners, the company previously withdrew fiscal 2025 guidance.

Fifth Third Bancorp Reports Third Quarter 2024 Earnings

Fifth Third Bancorp (NASDAQ: FITB) has reported robust earnings for the third quarter of 2024, demonstrating resilience in a challenging economic environment. The bank reported diluted earnings per share of $0.78, a decline of 4% from the previous quarter but an increase of 14% compared to the same period last year. Net interest income (FTE) was $1,427 million, up 2% from the prior quarter but down 1% from the year-ago quarter [2].

Fifth Third Bancorp's strong performance was driven by fee income growth and a resilient balance sheet. The bank's net interest margin (NIM) increased by 2 bps to 2.90%, while the efficiency ratio improved by 70 bps to 58.2%. The bank also executed a $200 million share repurchase and raised its common stock dividend by 6%.

Market Sentiment: 18% of Firms Anticipate Improved Trading in Third Quarter

According to a recent survey, 18% of firms anticipate improved trading conditions in the third quarter of 2025. This optimism is likely driven by the continued recovery of the economy and the positive financial results reported by major corporations like Kroger and Fifth Third Bancorp.

Conclusion

The financial performance of Kroger and Fifth Third Bancorp highlights the resilience of the retail and banking sectors. As the third quarter of 2025 approaches, investors can expect continued strong performance, supported by a positive market sentiment.
